- Deliver clear handoff materials and a playbook for transition to an AE or an ongoing hire.
- Coordinate closely with the founder or sole executive stakeholder throughout the engagement; focus on build, validate, and enable — not long-term sales management.
- Recommend tooling and operations improvements and optimize CRM/outbound tool usage; manage reasonable outbound tooling month-to-month (budget available).

- Proven RevOps / sales-ops / sales-enablement experience that includes building an outbound motion from near-zero — ideally at a consulting/implementation/services firm or large professional services organization.

### Role Summary

We are looking for a **GTM Engineer** to build the AI and automation that make ClickHouse's go-to-market motion faster, smarter, and more scalable. This is a builder role. You will design, build, and ship the systems, agents, and workflows that take manual work off the team and put usage and customer signals to work across the lifecycle. ClickHouse runs on a consumption model, where the returns from instrumenting and automating the customer journey are large and mostly uncaptured. This role exists to capture them.

### Responsibilities

- Design, build, and ship AI and automation across the GTM motion: prospecting and enrichment, lead routing and activation, outbound and follow-up, deal and technical sales support, and expansion and retention signals.
- Build agents and workflows that run reliably at scale and take repetitive work off Sales, Solutions Architecture, and Marketing.
- Instrument the customer lifecycle. Connect the GTM systems and data so usage and telemetry signals flow to the right place and trigger the right action automatically.
- Partner with the field to find where AI and automation create real gains, and turn those opportunities into systems people actually use.
- Own what you build end-to-end. Design it, deploy it, measure whether it moves a real number, and keep improving it. Stand up evals and monitoring so AI output stays reliable in production.
- Set the standards and guardrails for AI in GTM: data quality, prompt and eval discipline, human review where it matters, and controls that keep automated actions safe.
- Track the AI and automation tooling landscape and bring the best of it into how ClickHouse goes to market.

### Requirements/Qualifications

- 5+ years building automation and tooling in a GTM, RevOps, or growth engineering context, with systems you have shipped and run in production.
- Production experience with the GTM stack: Salesforce as the system of record, Gong and Gong Engage for conversation intelligence and sequencing, and the engineering layer beneath them: Vercel, Clay, n8n, enrichment providers, and both transactional and analytical databases (Postgres and ClickHouse). You have shipped and operated these in production at real scale.
- Hands-on development in Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript.
- Fluency with modern AI tooling: LLM APIs, agent and orchestration frameworks, prompting, evals, and retrieval with embeddings and vector search. You know how to get reliable behavior out of probabilistic systems, and you use eval and observability tooling like Langfuse to keep them reliable in production.
- Strong data-activation skills: SQL, APIs, and integrations, transformation with dbt, and moving warehouse data into the GTM stack and back.
- A builder who ships. You are comfortable owning something from idea to working system, and you measure it by whether it runs reliably and moves a real number.
- Owner-operator mindset. You treat what you build as a system you own end-to-end: you build it, you run it, you fix it when it breaks, and you keep making it better.
- Judgment about where AI and automation help and where they create risk. You know when to automate a workflow fully, when to keep a human in the loop, and when to leave a process alone.
- Familiarity with usage-based or consumption-based business models is a plus. You understand how usage and telemetry signals drive expansion and retention.
- Strong written and verbal communication. Comfortable partnering across the field and explaining what your systems do and why.
- Bachelor's degree in engineering required. A master's degree is a plus.

### Compensation

For roles based in the **United States**, the typical starting salary range for this position is $145,000 - $195,000 USD. In certain locations, such as the San Francisco Bay Area and the New York City Metro Area, a premium market range may apply, as listed. These salary ranges reflect what we reasonably and in good faith believe to be the minimum and maximum pay for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation may be higher or lower than the amounts listed, and the ranges may be subject to future adjustments. An individual’s placement within the range will depend on various factors, including (but not limited to) education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, location, performance, and the needs of the business or organization.

### Location/Workplace Type

Remote-friendly. ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and currently operates in over 20 countries.

# GTM Engineer
## Location
In person in New York City

## Employment Type
Full time

## Location Type
On-site

## What we're building
Mutiny is the self-improving AI infrastructure for GTM teams to execute faster and close more revenue. With Mutiny, everyone in sales and marketing gets a bench of GTM athletes that handle any work across their revenue motion and learn from what's actually moved their deals.

## The opportunity
Most GTM engineers wire up someone else's stack. You'll build a new one. As Mutiny's GTM engineer, you'll own the systems that power how we go to market, from outbound and onboarding to enrichment, routing, and the AI-native workflows that let a small team operate like a much bigger one. This role is in person in New York City, five days a week.

## What you'll own
- **Automations and internal tools.** Build the workflows and tools that make sales and marketing faster. The tool you ship today saves the team a week next month.
- **The plumbing.** APIs, data flows, integrations between every tool we run on. You make systems talk so the team doesn't have to.

## Who you are
- **A systems thinker.** You see one-off work and want to make it repeatable. You spot patterns and bottlenecks before they become someone's full-time problem.
- **A builder.** You've shipped automations, internal tools, and workflows that made a team measurably faster. You'd rather build than brief.
- **Comfortable with plumbing.** APIs, data flows, enrichment, routing. You know how to connect systems and make them work, even when the docs are wrong.
- **A cross-functional translator.** You can explain what you're building and why it matters to a CMO, a CRO, and an engineer in the same week. None of them feel talked down to.

Compensation Range: $150K - $250K

**Job Title:** Founding US Solutions Engineer

**Location:** New York City (On-Site)

**Compensation:** $180-220k OTE (uncapped) + Equity

**About Kombo:**
Kombo is the unified API for HR, payroll, Assessment, LMS and recruiting systems. Instead of spending months building integrations one by one, companies integrate once with Kombo and connect to 120+ platforms instantly.

**The Role:**
We're hiring our first US-based Solutions Engineer to own the technical relationship with customers - from first sales call through to successful implementation. You'll be the technical expert prospects and customers rely on to understand how Kombo fits their stack, design their integration approach, and get them live. You'll work closely with our Sales team, and our CRO to close deals and with Product/Engineering to turn customer insights into product improvements. This is a builder role. You'll help establish our US solutions team, create repeatable playbooks, and shape how we work with customers.

**Responsibilities:**
- **Own the technical sales cycle:** Lead discovery and demos, translating customer requirements into integration designs; Create technical proposals covering architecture, security, and implementation approach; Partner with AEs to close complex deals with engineering and executive stakeholders.
- **Drive implementations to go-live:** Own the technical relationship from POC to signed contract through production deployment; Build implementation plans, troubleshoot API issues, and unblock customers directly; Serve as the escalation point until customers are live and successful.
- **Build the technical toolkit:** Create demo environments, code samples (Python, Node.js), and Postman collections; Write integration guides, architecture diagrams, and troubleshooting documentation; Develop sales collateral: security questionnaire responses to technical one-pagers.
- **Scale the US solutions function:** Document repeatable playbooks for discovery, scoping, and implementation; Feed customer insights to Product/Engineering to shape the roadmap; Help define hiring and onboarding as we grow the team.

**Requirements/Qualifications:**
- 4+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or technical customer-facing roles at a B2B SaaS company.
- Hands-on experience with APIs - you can read documentation, write sample code, and debug integration issues.
- Track record working complex deals with technical and non-technical stakeholders - consistent deal value of $100k-150k+.
- Strong communication skills: you can whiteboard architecture with engineers and explain value to executives.
- Comfort with ambiguity and building things from scratch.

**Compensation:** $180-220k OTE (uncapped) + Equity

**Location/Workplace Type:** New York City (On-Site) 4+ days per week.

**Go-to-Market Engineer**

Revivn is a profitable and rapidly growing company that helps enterprises manage their technology through our end of life software platform. We take electronic recycling one step further by repurposing hardware that still has remaining life and providing it to people who lack dedicated computer access and make it more affordable for people who may not be able to purchase new technology. Working with companies like Instacart, Lyft, Qualtrics, X, Gensler, and Allbirds we are changing the way companies view used technology with a new model that focuses on repurposing instead of recycling.

We’re hiring our first Go-to-Market Engineer: a creative builder who sits between RevOps, marketing and full-stack engineering. Maybe you’re a computer science grad or early-career engineer who loves experimenting with tools and automation but doesn’t want to get lost in a giant company. You want to see the impact of what you build every day — on real leads, data, and revenue.

This is a hybrid technical + commercial role — ideal for someone who loves hacking together systems, writing quick scripts, and making data come alive. You’ll report into Marketing and collaborate closely with RevOps, Data, and Sales to automate workflows, enrich data, and make our GTM machine smarter, faster, and more creative.

**What You’ll Do**
- Build, scrape, and automate: Own the GTM automation and enrichment stack — from web scraping (Apify) to AI-driven enrichment (Hugging Face).
- Connect and create: Use APIs and lightweight code (Python, JavaScript) to glue together tools and make our data flow effortlessly.
- Experiment fast: Prototype workflows, test ideas, and turn what works into repeatable playbooks.
- Work across teams: Collaborate with Marketing, RevOps, and Sales to translate messy problems into automated systems.
- Push boundaries: Play with libraries like Crawlee, Cheerio, BeautifulSoup, Transformers, and Datasets to make research and enrichment faster.
- Stay curious: Constantly explore new AI, no-code, and automation tools — from Make and Zapier to emerging scrapers and APIs.
- Make GTM scale creatively: Build automations that still feel human — thoughtful, personal, and scalable.

**Who You Are**
- Creative problem-solver — you love finding clever shortcuts and unconventional ways to get things done.
- Early-career engineer, ideally with a CS or data-focused background, and eager to grow.
- In-between RevOps and full-stack: technical enough to code, curious enough to understand business context.
- Excited about tools: you tinker with APIs, scrape sites for fun, or wire up automations just to see what’s possible.
- Comfortable with ambiguity: you can turn loose ideas into structured systems.
- Fast learner and builder: you ship things quickly, break them, fix them, and learn.
- Motivated by impact: you want to see your work directly influence growth, pipeline, and revenue.

**Tech Stack**
- Languages: Python, JavaScript
- Web scraping: Apify, Crawlee, Cheerio, BeautifulSoup
- AI enrichment: Hugging Face, Transformers, Datasets
- Automation: Zapier, Make, Clay
- CRM and GTM stack: Salesforce, plus whatever creative tools you bring to the table.

**Perks**
- Competitive salary
- Direct impact: your work fuels meetings, pipeline, and revenue
- Ownership: this is a role built from the ground up – you’ll shape how GTM at Revivn evolves
- Growth environment: scrappy, fast-paced, feedback driven
- Collaboration with Sales, Data, RevOps, Engineering

If this sounds like you, apply! If you don’t meet all of the qualifications but think you could be a match, we’d still love the chance to review your application.

We embrace diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment. At Revivn, we encourage people from all ages, abilities, and experiences to apply. Revivn does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy or caregiver status, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

At Revivn, we prioritize transparency about our salary throughout the entire recruitment process. Be prepared to chat about compensation on your initial screen so that we can ensure alignment. If salary expectations and ranges are out of sync, we believe it is kind to respect everyone’s time and may discontinue conversations.

But, here at Revivn, we ALSO believe in investing in the lifetime value of each individual we meet and interact with. (We love knowing good humans and supporting them in whatever they do). We know that if it isn’t a good fit at the moment, it doesn’t necessarily mean that it won’t be a good fit in the future as we both continue to grow! We work to remain in contact with prospective candidates if the recruitment process ends early on.

For all job openings, we consider candidates with various backgrounds and levels of experience. When we give an offer it is based on individual skills and experience, as well as how that stacks up against other employees in the role. The salary range for a Go-to-Market Engineer is expected to be between **$85,000-120,000/year**. Your exact offer may vary based on these factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, and experience. The compensation package will also include comprehensive benefits such as medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with a 401(k) plan.

What Is a Career Ladder?

A career ladder, or career path, is a progression framework. It allows an organization to describe the different job levels and the expectations for a given position.

It enables the assessment of a software engineer's skills and to work on her career progression. It provides a shared framework to identify the different aspects to improve to reach the next job level.

The ladder can also be mapped with employee's compensation, increasing salaries transparency, and fairness.

Expertise Path and Manager Path (Dual-Track)

Most of the software engineering career ladders are dual tracks ladders.

They have a joint base for the first positions, and at some point, two paths are possible the expertise path and the people management path. The expertise path is often named the individual contributor track, the people management path is often called the manager track.

Mar 26 Sharing Our Engineering Ladder

Camille

I gave a talk last year at the NYC CTO summit on how and why to introduce structure into an engineering organization (slides available here). I am a fan of structure and the clarity that it can provide an organization, despite its potential downsides. I'm not going to talk about the WHY very much in this post, but I thought it was about time that I helped with the HOW.

Creating an engineering ladder (that is, the job descriptions and levels of an engineering organization) is a daunting task. If you do a half-hearted job, you're likely to cause more problems than you solve. The very first ladder I presented to my team was based on the ladder at Foursquare*. It was very simple, with one or two descriptive elements per "attribute" of engineering (technical skill, communication skill, etc), and by all accounts worked very well for their team. I hoped that this style of providing fewer details would result in people being less obsessed with the ladder, less likely to try to negotiate their level on "technicalities". Boy was I wrong. Almost immediately I had engineers debating me over whether they were at the right level, and there was a great deal of anxiety and confusion throughout the organization. I left room for generous interpretation, and it made it difficult for me to explain what I really wanted and expected.

snippet:
**Role Summary:**
We're hiring a Go-To-Market (GTM) Engineer to join the Growth organization, where you'll work directly with Sales, Marketing, RevOps, and beyond to translate GTM strategy into action by building systems, running experiments, activating signals, and scaling what works. This is a hands-on systems role. You'll design and ship the data pipelines, automation systems, scoring models, and AI-assisted workflows that power how Immuta identifies, reaches, and converts enterprise buyers. You won't be handing off requirements to an engineering team — you'll be writing the code, wiring the integrations, and owning the output end-to-end.

**Core Responsibilities:**
- **Signal Aggregation & Scoring Systems**
  - Build and maintain ICP scoring models, intent signal pipelines, and account prioritization logic sourced across our stack (Salesforce, Apollo, Warmly, Clay, and more)
  - Own the data transformation layer: pulling from CRM, enrichment APIs, and intent platforms, normalizing and enriching, and writing clean outputs back to Salesforce or downstream activation tools
  - Partner with RevOps on data definitions and quality to ensure scoring logic runs on trustworthy inputs

- **AI-Assisted GTM Workflows**
  - Apply LLMs to automate research, contact enrichment, signal extraction, and outreach personalization at scale
  - Design workflows that are measurable, testable, and repeatable — not one-off prompts
  - Reduce manual effort across Sales and Marketing by replacing high-frequency, low-complexity tasks with reliable automation

- **Middleware & Integration Infrastructure**
  - Build lightweight orchestration systems that connect GTM tools across the stack
  - Own the full lifecycle: standing up, maintaining, and iterating on integrations as the tool stack evolves
  - Know when to use n8n vs a custom FastAPI endpoint vs a scheduled Python job, and implement whichever is right

- **Experimentation & Measurement**
  - Build the scaffolding that lets the team run GTM experiments across audiences, channels, and messaging
  - Instrument experiments with enough signals to distinguish what's working from what's noise
  - Operationalize successful approaches by moving from one-off test to repeatable, scalable system

**Requirements/Qualifications:**
- **Experience:** 5+ years in Sales Ops, GTM Ops, RevOps, Marketing Ops, or a related technical role
- **Python:** Proficiency with pandas, data transformation pipelines, scoring model construction, and structured output formatting — comfortable owning a codebase, not just running scripts
- **Integration Engineering:** Hands-on experience building systems that ingest data from multiple sources, apply transformation logic at a midpoint layer, and route outputs to a destination (Zapier, n8n, or custom API orchestration)
- **Salesforce:** Strong data fluency — you know the object model, can write SOQL, and understand how CRM data needs to be structured to be usable downstream
- **Problem Solving:** Experience translating open-ended business questions into working systems with minimal specification; consulting, agency, or early-stage SaaS backgrounds are a strong fit
- **LLMs:** Familiarity with LLMs in production contexts — classification, extraction, summarization, and prompt chaining (not just vibe coding)

**Compensation:**
$115,000 - $140,000 a year. Additional compensation may include commission, variable pay, or equity, alongside benefits like healthcare, stock options, parental leave, unlimited paid time off, and learning resources.

**Location/Workplace Type:**
Austin, TX or Columbus, OH; Remote; Hybrid workplace.

snippet:
**About the Role**
As a GTM Engineer at Attentive, you will serve as an embedded technical builder within Revenue Operations, reporting to the VP of Revenue Operations. This role is designed to increase the speed, adaptability, and leverage of our go-to-market organization by building smart, lightweight solutions on top of our core systems landscape. You will partner closely with our RevTech team, which owns the foundational systems roadmap and long-term architecture, while operating in a distinct lane: moving quickly to solve high-value GTM problems that do not need to wait for the core roadmap. This includes designing and deploying fast, thoughtful solutions across workflow automation, data enrichment, AI-enabled processes, and bespoke internal tooling that reduce manual work and improve the quality of our go-to-market signals. This role is ideal for someone who is highly technical, pragmatic, and deeply motivated by shipping real solutions quickly. You should be excited by ambiguity, energized by business problems, and constantly looking for ways to make our teams faster, smarter, and more effective.

**What You’ll Accomplish**
- **Build fast, high-impact GTM solutions:** Design and ship workflows, automations, and internal tools that improve how our Sales and Customer Success teams operate day to day.
- **Reduce manual work across the GTM organization:** Eliminate repetitive rep and CSM tasks by automating data capture, field population, handoffs, enrichment, and workflow steps across tools like Salesforce, Gong, and other GTM systems.
- **Increase signal density and data usefulness:** Improve the quality of the data we collect and surface by auto-populating the fields that matter most, enriching customer and pipeline data, and making key signals easier for teams to act on.
- **Identify and deploy AI-enabled workflows:** Proactively explore how AI, agents, and automation platforms can improve go-to-market productivity, reduce operational burden, and create leverage before every underlying system is fully mature.
- **Operate with speed and pragmatism:** Build with a clear point of view on where speed matters most versus where durability and enterprise-grade tooling are required. Move quickly on bespoke internal workflows while partnering on more critical, cross-functional processes appropriately.
- **Self-source high-value opportunities:** Work directly with frontline teams and leaders across Sales, CS, and RevOps to identify friction, uncover inefficiencies, and generate a pipeline of projects that materially improve how the business runs.
- **Own outcomes, not tickets:** Drive work end-to-end from problem identification through implementation, adoption, and iteration—with success measured by business impact, speed, and usability.

**Your Expertise**
- **Strong experience building workflows, automations, or internal tools** in GTM, Revenue Operations, and adjacent technical roles, ideally in a high-growth SaaS environment.
- **2+ years of experience working across GTM systems** such as Salesforce, Gong, enrichment tools, and automation platforms, with a strong track record of improving process through systems.
- **Hands-on experience with GTM systems and automation tooling**, such as Salesforce, Gong, Zapier, enrichment platforms, AI workflow tools, or similar technologies.
- **Strong systems judgment**, including the ability to distinguish between workflows that should be solved through fast, bespoke builds versus those that require more durable, enterprise-grade solutions.
- **A high-agency builder mindset:** You are entrepreneurial, resourceful, and comfortable operating off-leash within clear swim lanes. You do not wait for perfect requirements to get started.
- **Demonstrated ability to move quickly and independently**, turning loosely defined business problems into practical, working solutions with limited oversight.
- **Fluency with AI tools and emerging automation capabilities,** along with genuine curiosity about how to apply them in practical ways to improve business operations.
- **Strong cross-functional instincts and communication skills,** with the ability to work directly with technical and non-technical stakeholders and quickly understand where pain exists.

**Compensation**
- The US base salary range for this full-time position is $140,000 - $175,000 annually + equity + benefits.

**Location/Workplace Type**
- United States.

**Role Overview**  
Databahn is looking for a Product Manager – Product Operations to drive operational rigor, pricing strategy, margin optimization, and roadmap governance across our Security Data Fabric platform.  
**This role blends:**  
• Product Operations leadership  
• Pricing and monetization ownership  
• Margin and cost-to-serve visibility  
• Core product management execution  
You will establish strong intake processes, govern roadmap prioritization, track POCs through production, and ensure visibility into cost-to-serve at customer and feature levels—while driving scalable pricing and healthy gross margins.  
This role is critical to ensuring Databahn scales efficiently, profitably, and predictably.  

**Key Responsibilities**  
1. **Product Operations Leadership**  
   - Own the centralized intake process for customer feature requests, sales-driven enhancements, and strategic initiatives.  
   - Define clear evaluation criteria across revenue impact, margin implications, cost-to-serve impact, and strategic alignment.  
   - Establish roadmap governance frameworks and prioritization cadences.  
   - Ensure trade-off transparency across Engineering, Finance, and Sales.  
   - Maintain visibility into committed vs exploratory work.  

   - Define and operationalize a structured POC lifecycle with qualification criteria, success metrics, engineering investment thresholds, and exit criteria.  
   - Track all POCs from inception through technical validation, commercial validation, and production deployment.  
   - Measure conversion rate from POC to production, engineering effort vs revenue realized, and margin impact of custom implementation.  
   - Build frameworks to quantify cost-to-serve across data ingestion, storage, compute, routing & enrichment, and customer-specific configurations.  
   - Develop dashboards to track cost per GB ingested, cost per routing workload, and cost per customer segment.  
   - Partner with Finance to align pricing with infrastructure realities and track gross margin by feature and customer.  

2. **Pricing Strategy & Monetization**  
   - Own Databahn’s pricing and packaging strategy.  
   - Design scalable pricing models aligned to data ingestion volume, throughput, transformation workloads, and infrastructure cost drivers.  
   - Conduct pricing experiments and elasticity analysis.  
   - Partner with Sales on enterprise deal structuring.  
   - Support custom pricing models while protecting margin integrity.  
   - Conduct win/loss analysis with pricing competitiveness insights.  

3. **Margin Optimization**  
   - Analyze cost drivers across data ingestion, storage, compute, and routing and enrichment.  
   - Collaborate with Engineering to improve architectural efficiency, reduce infra spend per workload, and increase automation.  
   - Identify and execute initiatives that expand gross margins.  
   - Track and improve margin performance at feature level, customer segment level, and enterprise account level.  

4. **Core Product Management**  
   - Own roadmap prioritization balancing revenue impact, margin expansion, customer enhancements, and strategic platform investments.  
   - Translate pricing and operational insights into clear product requirements.  
   - Drive structured PRD creation and release documentation.  
   - Use modern AI-assisted tools to accelerate documentation, analyze customer feedback, model pricing scenarios, and summarize operational datasets.  
   - Ensure high execution velocity with operational discipline.  

5. **Customer & Market Engagement**  
   - Work closely with Sales to structure large enterprise deals.  
   - Monitor trends across security data platforms, SIEM vendors, and observability pipelines.  
   - Maintain awareness of AWS, GCP, and Azure cost structures.  
   - Partner with Customer Success on renewal strategy, expansion pricing, and margin protection in upsells.  

6. **Cross-Functional Leadership**  
   - Collaborate deeply with Engineering, Finance, Sales, and Customer Success.  
   - Serve as the internal authority on product monetization, cost-to-serve economics, operational product governance, pricing strategy, and margin health.  

**Minimum Qualifications**  
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field  
- 6+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, infrastructure, or platform products  
- Experience in Product Operations, roadmap governance, or revenue operations alignment  
- Experience in security, SIEM, or observability platforms  
- Strong analytical skills with experience in pricing and margin analysis  
- Understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and cloud-native architectures  
- Experience owning cross-functional execution across Engineering, Sales, and Finance  
- Strong written communication skills and experience creating PRDs  
- Experience using AI-assisted tools in product workflows  

**Preferred Qualifications**  
- Experience in usage-based SaaS pricing models  
- Experience in observability platforms  
- Familiarity with cloud cost modeling (AWS, GCP, Azure)  
- MBA or background in finance or business strategy  
- Startup experience in high-growth, high-scale environments  

**Why This Role Matters**  
Databahn operates in a data-intensive domain where infrastructure efficiency, pricing precision, and operational discipline directly determine profitability.  
This role ensures:  
- POCs convert into scalable revenue  
- Roadmaps are governed by economic reality  
- Cost-to-serve is visible and optimized  
- Pricing becomes a strategic advantage  
You will help build not just a product—but a financially durable, operationally disciplined platform built for scale.

Plane sells to engineering, product, and IT teams, and to buyers with real compliance and self-hosting needs. These people delete generic outreach on sight. Your job is to make outbound specific enough, timed well enough, and relevant enough that a skeptical technical buyer replies.

- Use LLMs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and others to research accounts and personalize at scale
- Turn Plane's signals into trigger-based plays: GitHub activity, Docker pulls, self-host installs, community engagement, funding, hiring, and tech-stack changes
- Keep the CRM clean and in sync with your data and sequencing layers
- Track reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked, pipeline created, and cost per meeting

**Role Summary**
We're looking for a GTM Engineer to build and operate the automated systems that power Gumloop's revenue engine. You'll focus on three areas first and foremost: sales outbound, marketing automation, and. This is an individual contributor role on a GTM function that exists but is still in its earliest days, so you'll have a real greenfield opportunity to shape how we work.

**Responsibilities**
- Build the GTM engine on Gumloop: Design and deploy AI agents and workflows that automate our own go-to-market, from signal-based prospecting and enrichment to meeting scheduling, CRM hygiene, and post-call follow-ups. Dogfood the platform harder than anyone.
- Connect the full GTM stack: Integrate Salesforce, Clay, Apollo, and other tools into a cohesive system where data flows cleanly between them. Build the enrichment logic, sync architecture, and routing rules that keep everything accurate and deduplicated.
- Own and build inside Salesforce: Take ownership of the objects, fields, tables, flows, automations, validation rules, and integrations that keep our revenue motion running cleanly - and give every GTM team the structure and clean data they need to execute.
- Automate sales outbound: Build the outbound engine end-to-end, covering intent detection, account enrichment, AI-personalized touchpoints, human review checkpoints, and CRM sync, all wired to a single output: qualified meetings on the calendar.
- Automate marketing and CS workflows: Ship playbooks for lifecycle marketing, lead scoring, churn-risk alerts, onboarding sequences, and customer health monitoring. Turn manual, repetitive work across marketing and CS into automated systems.
- Partner with GTM leadership to turn strategy into systems: Work directly with sales, marketing, and CS leadership to translate go-to-market strategy into automated playbooks, dynamic scoring models, and signal-driven workflows that produce measurable revenue outcomes.
- Own data quality and governance: Build the validation rules, deduplication logic, and data structure that the rest of the GTM stack depends on, so every team can trust the data they're working from.
- Build for reliability and document your work: Design observability, monitoring, and debugging into the systems you build to keep them running at high uptime, and document what you ship so others can understand, trust, and extend it.
- Influence the product: Your experience automating Gumloop's own GTM is a direct input to product development. Surface friction, propose features, and help shape what we build next.

**Requirements/Qualifications**
- Technical aptitude: You're comfortable working with APIs, webhooks, data integrations, and SQL. You can write scripts to connect systems and manipulate data. You don't need to be an advanced coder, but you think in systems and can build automations from scratch.
- 3+ years in a GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, Revenue Operations, or technical RevOps role where you worked closely with sales, marketing, or CS teams. We're also open to people from adjacent technical roles who want to move into GTM.
- GTM fluency: You understand the sales funnel, CRM data models (Salesforce, HubSpot), enrichment ecosystems (Clay, Apollo, 6sense), and how revenue teams actually work day-to-day. You can speak the language of AEs, SDRs, and CSMs.

**Senior RevOps Analyst**

**LOCATION:** Lehi, UT

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**
As our Senior Revenue Operations Analyst, you’ll help drive results across the systems and processes that keep revenue moving. On the RevOps side, you’ll turn data into clean pipelines, sharp reporting, and smarter processes that help the sales team perform. On the Deal Desk side, you’ll help deals move cleanly from quote to signature to billing. The two go hand in hand — better data and process make for smoother deals, and well-run deals keep the data clean. You’ll do this alongside a RevOps team and close partners in Sales, Systems, and Finance. If you like driving pipeline to revenue and helping a team close with confidence, this role is for you.

- **Sales process improvement.** Map current sales and handoff processes, find the friction, and design cleaner workflows, automations, and playbooks in HubSpot that help reps sell faster and more consistently.

- **Quote-to-cash process.** Keep the handoff from closed-won to billing and finance clean — order accuracy, correct effective dates, and tight sync between HubSpot and the billing system.

- **Tech Stack management.** Help administer the revenue tech stack (HubSpot, Gong, and connected tools); maintain documented SOPs.

- Experience with quotes, contracts, or order management, and comfort owning quote-to-cash mechanics.

- Clear communicator who can turn analysis into recommendations leadership can act on.
- Self-starter who takes ownership of their area and thrives in a fast-moving, results-driven environment.
- Bonus: experience with DocuSign, QuotaPath, Gong, Clay, or other similar tools.

**Role Overview:**
The Fractional CFO role at Meyer Wilson Werning exists to provide the strategic financial leadership the firm currently does not have in-house. This is not a full-time CFO role, and it is not a bookkeeping or day-to-day accounting position. The firm already has a trusted Office Administrator/Bookkeeper who manages day-to-day financial operations, along with an external CPA firm that handles tax preparation.

The need is for a sophisticated financial professional who can help firm leadership interpret clean, reliable financial data, improve budgeting and forecasting, create digestible reporting, analyze profitability, identify operational inefficiencies, and support proactive financial decision-making. Because Meyer Wilson Werning operates on a plaintiff-side contingency-fee model, the right candidate must understand the challenge of variable revenue, no recurring revenue, no traditional accounts receivable, long case timelines, and cash flow planning around major case wins or losses.

**What you'll do:**
- **Strategic Financial Leadership:** Provide high-level financial strategy and advisory support to help the firm make proactive business decisions.
- **Budgeting & Forecasting:** Build budgeting and forecasting processes that reflect the realities of a contingency-fee law firm with variable monthly revenue.
- **Cash Flow Planning:** Help firm leadership understand monthly operating needs, payroll stability, cash flow timing, and the impact of case wins or losses.
- **Financial Reporting:** Translate existing financial data into clear, digestible, executive-level reports that the firm owner and Office Administrator/Bookkeeper can use for decision-making.
- **Profitability Analysis:** Analyze operating expenses, profit margins, spending patterns, and opportunities to improve efficiency.
- **Scenario Planning:** Help leadership plan around revenue variability, major case outcomes, tax considerations, and future financial needs.
- **Tax Strategy Coordination:** Work with the external CPA firm to identify tax planning opportunities and support more strategic tax-related decision-making.
- **Dashboard & KPI Development:** Create dashboards, KPIs, or reporting frameworks that give leadership better visibility into firm performance.
- **Technology & Process Review:** Assess current tools, including Litify, Accounting Seed, Excel, and existing reporting processes, then recommend practical improvements where needed.
- **Strategic Partnership:** Work directly with the firm owner and Office Administrator/Bookkeeper as the third member of the firm's financial leadership structure.

**What we're looking for:**
- **Fractional CFO Experience:** Prior experience as a Fractional CFO or senior finance leader advising business owners, ideally small to medium size law firms.
- **Plaintiff Contingency-Fee Understanding:** Strong preference for experience with plaintiff-side contingency-fee law firms or professional services businesses with variable revenue.
- **Strategic Finance Expertise:** Strong background in financial strategy, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow modeling, profitability analysis, and executive reporting.
- **Executive Communication:** Ability to explain financial information clearly, translate data into recommendations, and help leadership make proactive decisions.
- **High Integrity & Discretion:** Able to handle confidential financial information with professionalism and trustworthiness.
- **Data-Driven Mindset:** Comfortable working with clean financial data and turning it into practical business insight.
- **Tool Familiarity:** Experience with Excel and financial reporting tools required; familiarity with Litify and Accounting Seed is strongly preferred but not required.
- **Advisory Orientation:** Best suited for someone who enjoys strategic advisory work rather than transactional bookkeeping or routine accounting tasks.
- **Fractional Fit:** Must be comfortable with a true fractional engagement of approximately 10–15 hours per month, with potentially more involvement during onboarding.

**Work Arrangement:**
Remote position, fully flexible engagement structured as a monthly retainer for defined hours.

**Compensation:**
Structured as a monthly retainer for defined hours, offering stable and predictable income. Compensation tailored to market standards for fractional CFO roles.

München, DE

## The Role
This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of GTM and AI. You build the systems that help Sales, Marketing, and CS work on the right things: automated lead identification, scoring models that flag retention risks before anyone notices them, LLM pipelines, custom integrations. You own what you build end-to-end - scoping, shipping, keeping it running. You work closely with GTM Leadership.

## What You'll Do
- **Source pipeline from external data:** Scrape and process signals from outside the CRM - news, public records, company announcements - and integrate them back into the CRM, the place where Sales Reps work.
- **Build scoring and enrichment systems:** Retention risk, account health, lead scoring: models that pull from transcripts, tickets, emails, and external data to give teams early signals on what needs attention.
- **Write the automation no tool covers:** You bring n8n or make.com workflows to the next level. Python scripts, LLM pipelines, vector databases, API integrations to get the best outcome.
- **Keep the revenue infrastructure running:** The data flows, enrichment logic, and integrations between tools that don't connect natively. You own the technical layer and keep it working as the stack grows.

## What We're Looking For
- You have a technical degree. Business Informatics, Information Systems, Computer Science, or similar. You're at home in both the data and the business context.
- Python is your default for anything complex. You write scripts, pipelines, and integrations from scratch and know when no-code is the right call and when it isn't.
- You feel comfortable with AI. You've built LLM pipelines, vector databases, RAG, sentiment analyses. You understand how these systems behave in practice, not just in theory.
- You're comfortable with unstructured data: transcripts, scraped articles, emails. Extracting a usable signal from a messy input is a normal part of your work.
- You're fluent in German and English. You'll move between both daily, with the team and across the company.

## What we offer
- **Your success pays off:** With our VSOP, you share in Alasco’s long-term success. If we grow together, you benefit too.

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those

**Type**: Contract/1099

### Role Overview

At Via Logic, we believe strong operations make meaningful work possible. As a growing small business supporting federal and commercial clients, our operating needs span people and talent, finance, contracts, compliance, security, delivery operations, partnerships, and internal systems. We're looking for a seasoned fractional Chief Operating Officer to serve as a high-level strategic advisor to Via Logic's principal and founders. This individual will provide executive guidance on organizational growth, mergers and acquisitions, strategic positioning, operational maturity, and long-term business planning. The role will work closely with leadership to assess opportunities, identify risks, advise on structure and sequencing, and help prepare the company for potential transactions, partnerships, expansion, or other significant growth initiatives. This is primarily an executive advisory engagement, with limited hands-on support for selected strategic and operational priorities based on agreed scope, available hours, and leadership needs.

In this role, you will provide executive-level guidance across several operating areas, with priorities selected and sequenced based on the company's most significant strategic and operational needs.

- Support planning around performance reviews, compensation cycles, benefits decisions, team lead structures, growth frameworks, succession planning, and workforce readiness.
- Help clarify which responsibilities should sit with People/Talent, leadership, internal operations, outside advisors, or other functional owners.
- Provide limited project-based support for selected People and Talent initiatives when agreed upon within the approved scope.

#### Expanse

- Advise on vendor relationships, consultant support, strategic partnerships, and other external business relationships.
- Help leadership evaluate partnership opportunities, operational dependencies, risks, ownership considerations, and expected business value.

#### Finance

## About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on RevOps/GTM engineer to own the revenue systems layer across a genuinely messy and interesting go-to-market. You'll design and maintain the pipes connecting CRM, billing, warehouse, and analytics, and wire AI into the workflows in between. You'll work directly with revenue leadership and have wide latitude in how things get built.

**Why This Role Is Harder Than It Sounds**

- **The account hierarchy is real.** Our market spans solo practices, multi-location companies, roll-up brands, and PE platforms. The HubSpot company object has to do quadruple duty — PE firm → brand → company → location — with clean parent-child associations, dedup logic that respects the hierarchy, and reporting that rolls up correctly at every level.

- **Four GTM motions run in parallel.** SMB, mid-market, enterprise, and partner led — each needs its own routing, lifecycle logic, handoffs, and funnel reporting, without forking the CRM into four incompatible systems.

- **Three products, three pricing models.** Subscription, usage-based, and percentage-of-collections billing all flow through the same revenue stack. Normalizing these into coherent ARR/NRR, cohort, and revenue reporting is a core design problem, not an afterthought.

## About You

- You're a hands-on RevOps/GTM engineer with a builder profile.

- Strong SQL from scratch.

- You know when a Zap is enough and when it's time to write code.

- Self-directed; comfortable operating fractionally with async communication and minimal oversight.

## What We're Looking For

**Must-Haves**

- 4+ years in RevOps, GTM engineering, or sales/marketing ops with a builder profile.

- Deep, hands-on HubSpot experience custom objects, associations, workflows, API —ideally with complex parent-child account structures (multi-location, franchise, healthcare, or roll-up environments).

- Production experience with Stripe data, including usage-based or non-standard billing models.

- Production experience with Zapier.

- Practical experience building with Claude or comparable LLM APIs, prompting, evaluation, and knowing the failure modes.

- Self-directed; comfortable operating fractionally with async communication and minimal oversight.

**Nice-to-Haves**

- Healthcare or vertical SaaS experience; familiarity with provider data (NPI/NPPES, CMS datasets).

- Experience supporting multiple concurrent GTM motions (PLG/SMB velocity alongside enterprise sales).

- dbt and enrichment tooling (Apollo).

## What You'll Do

- **CRM architecture (HubSpot):** The parent-child company model, lifecycle stages, lead routing by segment, workflows, dedup, and data hygiene. You keep the CRM trustworthy so pipeline numbers are real at both the location and parent level.

- **Billing-to-CRM sync (Stripe):** Reconcile heterogeneous billing data (subscription, usage, % of collections) with CRM records; surface churn, expansion, and payment signals where the revenue team can act on them.

- **Automation (Zapier + scripting):** Build and maintain the integration layer. Know when a Zap is enough and when it's time to write code.

- **Data warehouse (Snowflake):** Model GTM and revenue data into clean, queryable tables that handle the hierarchy and mixed pricing models. Strong SQL from scratch.

- **Analytics (Metabase):** Dashboards leadership actually uses funnel conversion by motion, pipeline coverage, revenue normalized across pricing models, rollups by parent account.

- **AI workflows (Claude):** Lead enrichment and scoring, call summarization, follow-up drafting, and data cleanup at scale, including provider-level enrichment from industry datasets (NPI/NPPES).

**Compensation & Benefits**

- Industry-leading compensation, including salary and equity ownership.
- MacBook, monitor, and all the technologies you need to succeed.
- Full Medical & Dental Insurance.
- Unlimited PTO.
- 401k.
- Remote first company.
- Fast-paced startup environment.

- Employment Type: Contract (Part-Time)

We're looking for a fractional Insurance Advisor who has stood up an agency before and can tell us, quickly and directly, how to stand up ours. Abode is in the licensing process across ten states and building toward our own agency, which means a run of consequential decisions ahead of us on aggregators, carriers, systems, and structure.

## What You'll Do
- **Know-how on Agency Structure and Licensing:** Entity setup, the DRLP arrangement, and the order to sequence multi-state licensing so nothing sits blocked.
- **Guide Aggregator and Carrier Strategy:** Which aggregator to sign, which carriers to pursue first, and how to handle carriers who decline to appoint us.
- **Call the Vendor Decisions:** AMS, comparative rater, and data providers. Tell us when a choice is wrong before we build on top of it.
- **Shape the Referral to Agency Transition:** How to move from affiliate economics to owning the book without breaking the customer experience.
- **Design the Operating Model:** What servicing looks like at volume, the staffing ratios that hold, and what to expect on retention.
- **Set Compliance Guardrails:** What we can say and do before appointments land.
- **Pressure-test the Plan:** Review our assumptions and tell us where we're wrong.

## Who You Are
- You are the person insurance operators call when they're about to make an expensive mistake.
- You've built or run an agency yourself, and you're an expert.
- Your knowledge is current. You know which aggregators are appointing today and which systems break at volume.

## Basic Qualifications
- This role is remote and fractional. We intend for it to be 10hrs/week, 40hrs/month.
- Active or recent P&C license, with experience holding or supporting agency licensure across multiple states.
- You have personally stood up or run an independent agency, including carrier appointments and an aggregator or cluster relationship.
- Hands-on experience selecting and implementing an agency management system and comparative rater.
- Recent operating experience, so your answers reflect how carriers and aggregators behave today.
- Written disclosure of any compensation you receive from aggregators, carriers, AMS vendors, or data providers.

## Employment Details
- **Location:** Remote (United States)
- **Employment Type:** Full time
- **Department:** New Products
- **Location Type:** Remote

**Product Manager - Founding Team [RevOps Experience]**
**Location:** Bengaluru  
**Employment Type:** Full time  
**Location Type:** On-site

### 🎉 Job Description:
### 🎉 What will you be working on?
We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to join our early product team and own the **RevOps experience** on Reo - helping GTM teams turn raw signals into pipeline they can act on.

Reo pulls together millions of data points - firmographics, technographics, hiring signals, developer activity, and more - into a signal universe that GTM teams use to find and prioritize the right accounts.

Your job is to make that intelligence _usable_: helping RevOps and sales users build lead pipelines, segment accounts on dozens of attributes, and act on signals without drowning in data.

You’ll:
- Own the end-to-end experience of **signal-based pipeline building** - from "here's a pile of account data" to "here's my prioritized list to work this week".
- Design and iterate on **segmentation workflows** - letting users slice accounts by signals, firmographics, tech stack, and other attributes, without needing to be a data analyst to do it.
- Talk to RevOps and sales users constantly - understand how they currently build lists and pipeline (spreadsheets, CRM views, manual research) and translate that into product decisions.
- Dig into usage data yourself (query logs, product analytics) to spot friction points, drop-offs, and what "good" segmentation looks like.
- Work closely with engineering & design to ship fast, test with users, and iterate.
- Write clear specs and help keep the team aligned on priorities and what's shipping next.
- Ruthlessly prioritize - know which segmentation/pipeline improvements move usage and retention, and cut what doesn't.

### 👯 Skills we are looking for in this role:
- 2-4 years of Product Management experience, ideally in an early-stage or fast-moving tech startup, owning a feature area end-to-end.
- Comfort with **data-heavy or workflow-heavy products** - you've worked on something where the hard part was making a lot of structured/unstructured data usable, not just building a linear feature.
- Experience in building AI-native user experiences.
- Basic fluency with data - you can read a SQL query, sanity-check a metric, or work with a CSV export without needing someone else to translate it for you.
- Bias to ship - you'd rather get something in front of users this week and iterate than perfect it in a vacuum.

**Compensation:** Not specified.

**Job Title:** Senior Endpoint Systems Engineer  
**Location:** Hybrid: Chicago, IL  
**Job Type:** Full-Time  
**Salary:** $130,000 - $145,000 ANNUALLY  
**About the Role:**  
We are seeking a highly skilled and strategic Senior Endpoint Systems Engineer to join our IT team. In this role, you will serve as the primary architect and technical lead for the health, security, compliance, and lifecycle management of our global endpoint fleet.  
Our environment features a balanced mix of both Windows and macOS devices. We need a senior professional with deep, dual-platform expertise who can design scalable deployment workflows, architect robust endpoint security configurations, and optimize our enterprise toolset—specifically Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, and Workspace ONE. As a senior member of the team, you will drive technical strategy, lead complex integration projects, and mentor junior IT staff to ensure a seamless and secure digital employee experience.  
**Key Responsibilities:**  
- Architect, optimize, and maintain our global Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) infrastructure using Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, and VMware Workspace ONE.  
- Design and scale automated deployment, provisioning, and configuration management workflows for Windows 10/11 and macOS hardware.  
- Standardize and evolve modern deployment frameworks utilizing Windows Autopilot, Apple Business Manager (ABM), and Automated Device Enrollment to achieve zero-touch provisioning.  
- Develop, test, and maintain robust code repositories (PowerShell for Windows; Bash/Zsh/Python for macOS) to automate complex administrative tasks, custom reporting, and API integrations.  
- Partner closely with the Security team to engineer and enforce endpoint security baselines (e.g., CIS Benchmarks), disk encryption protocols (BitLocker, FileVault), and EDR/antivirus agent deployments.  
- Lead the integration of endpoint platforms with enterprise identity and access management (IAM) systems (e.g., Entra ID, Okta), including modern single sign-on (SSO) extensions.  
- Act as the highest tier of technical escalation for complex endpoint, OS, and software issues. Provide mentorship, guidance, and technical training to Tier 1/2 service desk and junior systems administrators.  
- Maintain a forward-looking roadmap for endpoint technologies, evaluate emerging tools, and author authoritative architectural diagrams and standard operating procedures (SOPs).  
**Required Skills & Qualifications:**  
- 5–8+ years of dedicated experience in endpoint engineering, systems administration, or infrastructure architecture within an enterprise environment.  
- Comprehensive, expert-level knowledge of both Windows and macOS operating systems, system internals, and enterprise deployment methodologies.  
- Deep hands-on engineering experience configuring and managing Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, and Workspace ONE at scale.  
- Strong proficiency in PowerShell and Bash/Zsh (Python or Swift is a significant plus) for advanced automation, custom scripts, and utilizing MDM APIs.  
- Proven ability to lead projects independently, collaborate across multi-functional engineering teams, and explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
title: Senior Endpoint Systems Engineer

**Location:** Los Angeles, California, United States  
**Work Arrangement:** Hybrid  
**Employment Type:** Full-time  
**Salary:** $85K–$105K USD per year + Comprehensive Benefits  
  
**About TubeScience**  
At TubeScience, we create data-driven video ads for some of the largest advertisers on Facebook and Instagram across fashion, beauty, food, fitness, healthcare, financial services, and more. We move quickly, test constantly, and use performance data to understand what audiences respond to. Our model is simple: clients only pay us when our videos outperform what they are already running internally.  
  
**The Role**  
As a Lead Editor, you’ll be the creative anchor of your pod. You’ll set the visual standard, guide editors toward stronger work, and help turn campaign strategy into high-performing creative. You’ll still be close to the craft, especially on high-priority campaigns, but your impact will go beyond your own edits.  
Your feedback will shape the quality of the team. Your judgment will influence how work gets made. And your leadership will help editors improve faster and make better creative decisions. You’ll also work closely with Creative Directors on team performance, workflow improvements, and your own growth as a leader.  
  
**What You’ll Do**  
- **Raise the Creative Bar:** Set quality standards, give feedback that’s actionable and grounded in what drives results, and step into high-priority edits when needed.  
- **Lead Your Pod:** Evaluate editors, identify capability gaps, and own staffing decisions — building and developing the strongest possible team to drive post-production output.  
- **Maximize Every Asset:** Review footage, curate strong selects, maintain organized libraries, and find smart ways to repurpose content.  
- **Bridge Production and Post:** Partner closely with Production on footage quality — flagging issues early and delivering feedback that’s actionable and consumer-minded.  
- **Partner with Strategy:** Share performance insights and strengthen knowledge-sharing between editorial and Strategy to keep creative decisions grounded in what’s working.  
- **Lead with a Business Mindset:** Represent editorial in cross-functional conversations, balance creative ambition with production realities, and make tough calls — on scope, timelines, or team assignments — when it’s what the work needs.  
- **Improve the Process:** Streamline workflows, explore new tools and AI capabilities, and bring solutions to recurring challenges.  
  
**Who You Are**  
- Strong visual judgment and a clear understanding of what makes an edit work  
- Ability to give clear, actionable feedback that editors can apply quickly  
- Strong understanding of how creative decisions connect to performance  
- Ability to guide and develop editors, holding the team accountable while building a strong roster  
- Sound business judgment — able to see the bigger picture across creative and team needs, and act decisively in a fast-paced, high-output environment  
- Willingness to stay hands-on when the work needs senior-level attention  
  
**Requirements:**  
- 7+ years of professional video editing experience  
- 3+ years in a managerial or leadership role  
- Expert-level proficiency in Premiere Pro and Adobe Creative Suite  
- Strong knowledge of After Effects and motion graphics  
- Experience in performance marketing, a creative agency, or an in-house creative team  
  
**Why TubeScience**  
- Your work goes live fast — no slow cycles  
- Learn performance marketing at scale  
- Work with a global, high-performing creative team  
  
**Benefits**  
- Health, Vision & Dental coverage  
- Unlimited PTO  
- 401(k) + Matching  
- Life Insurance  
- Paid Sick Days  
- Paid Parental Leave  
- And more!

snippet:
**POSITION SUMMARY**
The GTM Engineer is responsible for designing, building, and operating the technical infrastructure that powers EnableComp's account-based demand generation motion. This role sits at the intersection of Revenue Operations and Marketing, translating buying signals, catalysts, and triggers (M&A activity, leadership changes, RCM technology contract expirations, RFP activity, hiring patterns, and other intent data) into prioritized, enriched, and routed target accounts inside HubSpot. The GTM Engineer owns the tooling, data pipelines, and workflow automation connecting Clay, HubSpot, and other GTM systems, ensuring Marketing and Sales are always working the highest-propensity accounts with accurate, enriched data and minimal manual effort.

### The Job Responsibilities Include
- Build and maintain automated workflows in Clay that identify and score ABM signals, catalysts, and triggers (e.g., executive changes, M&A, technology contract expirations, RFPs, hiring surges) across target health system and physician group accounts.
- Partner with Marketing and Revenue Operations to design and maintain the HubSpot architecture (lists, workflows, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, and routing rules) that operationalizes signal-based account prioritization.
- Develop and maintain integrations and data pipelines between Clay, HubSpot, enrichment/intent data providers, and internal systems (e.g., CRM, data warehouse) using APIs, webhooks, and native connectors.
- Analyze account and contact-level data to identify patterns in signal quality, conversion, and pipeline impact, refining scoring models and enrichment logic accordingly.
- Lead the technical build-out of net-new ABM campaigns, ensuring signal capture, enrichment, and routing logic are in place before launch.
- Conduct regular audits of data quality, deduplication, and enrichment accuracy across HubSpot and Clay to maintain a clean, reliable source of truth for GTM teams.
- Coordinate with Sales Development, Partnerships, and Client Services to ensure signal-qualified accounts are routed to the right owner with appropriate context and timing.
- Evaluate new GTM tools, data providers, and automation opportunities that could improve signal detection, targeting precision, or operational efficiency.
- Identify gaps or bottlenecks in the demand generation tech stack and workflows, and design scalable solutions in partnership with Marketing and RevOps leadership.

### Requirements & Qualifications
- Education Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field required; equivalent practical experience considered
- 3+ years of experience in a GTM Engineering, Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or Sales Operations role, ideally within B2B SaaS or healthcare technology
- Demonstrated hands-on expertise administering HubSpot (workflows, lists, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, reporting) in a marketing or revenue operations capacity
- Direct experience building enrichment and signal-detection workflows in Clay, including use of formulas, integrations, and waterfall enrichment
- Working knowledge of APIs, webhooks, and no-code/low-code automation tools (e.g., Zapier, Make) to connect GTM systems
- Familiarity with account-based marketing (ABM) concepts, intent data providers, and B2B enterprise buying committees
- Strong SQL or spreadsheet-based data analysis skills; comfort working with large, imperfect data sets
- Timely and regular attendance.
- Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered
- To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

### Special Considerations & Prerequisites
- Minimal travel required (less than 20%), primarily for occasional team or company offsites
- Ability to work at a computer for extended periods; standard office or remote work environment
- A great candidate is self-directed and comfortable owning ambiguous, cross-functional problems; treats data hygiene as non-negotiable; and can translate technical workflows into plain-language impact for Sales and Marketing stakeholders
- Practices and adheres to EnableComp’s Core Values, Vision, and Mission.

**Location:** Remote in Canada

## Position Overview

We're looking for a Staff Platform Engineer to define and lead platform engineering strategy across complex, multi-environment cloud systems. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer who can own infrastructure architecture end-to-end, drive DevSecOps and compliance practices, and serve as a technical leader on the engagements they support.

In this role, you will work as a key technical contributor on a cross-functional team, defining standards and owning platform reliability, performance, and security at scale. You'll mentor engineers, partner with leadership on infrastructure direction, and lead complex migrations and modernization initiatives.

## What You'll Do

### Craft & Delivery

- Define DevOps strategy and lead infrastructure architecture across multi-environment, multi-region cloud systems

## Principal Architect – Digital Banking & Credit Union Transformation

**Location:** Remote

**Employment Type:** Contracted to Full Time

**Level:** Experienced

### The Opportunity

Aequilibrium is looking for a **Principal Digital Banking Architect** (contract-to-hire) to help lead the next generation of digital banking transformation for Canadian credit unions. This is not simply an architecture role. We are looking for a senior technology leader who can sit alongside a credit union CIO or CTO, understand their business and technology landscape, define the path from current to future state, and lead multidisciplinary teams through complex digital banking transformations.

### What You'll Lead

- Own architecture and technical leadership for complex digital banking transformations, including **Forge-to-VeriPark migrations**.
- Assess current-state environments and define target-state and transition architectures across digital banking, core banking, integration, cloud, data, identity, security and third-party systems.
- Lead architecture for **VeriChannel, VeriLink, Microsoft Azure and Dynamics 365/Power Platform ecosystems**.
- Establish integration and API strategies that connect digital banking platforms with core banking, payments, CRM, identity, fraud, analytics, and other financial-services systems.
- Lead Design Authority and architecture governance across Aequilibrium, client and vendor teams.
- Translate complex technical decisions into clear business implications for CIOs, CTOs and other executives.
- Guide engineering teams from architecture through implementation, testing, migration and go-live.
- Champion **configuration over customization**, platform upgradeability, security by design and API-first integration.
- Mentor solution architects, technical leads and engineers.

### Help Build Our Digital Banking Practice

Beyond individual projects, you will help shape Aequilibrium's digital banking architecture capability.

You will:

- Develop reusable reference architectures, migration playbooks, integration patterns and accelerators.
- Help define Aequilibrium's point of view on digital banking modernization and platform migration.
- Participate in strategic pursuits, client workshops and technical presentations.
- Build trusted relationships across the Canadian credit union ecosystem and with platform and technology partners.
- Contribute to thought leadership through articles, webinars, conferences, and industry discussions.
- Help identify emerging opportunities as credit unions modernize legacy platforms, consolidate through mergers, and collaborate through shared technology models.

### What We're Looking For

- **12+ years** in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, or senior technology leadership.
- Significant experience within **Canadian credit unions, banking, or financial services**.
- Proven leadership of at least one major digital banking modernization, platform migration, or comparable enterprise transformation from strategy through implementation.
- Strong understanding of digital banking architecture, core banking integration, payments, identity, security, and member-facing digital channels.
- Deep expertise in APIs, microservices, event-driven architecture, and enterprise integration.
- Strong Microsoft Azure architecture experience.
- Ability to move comfortably between executive strategy and detailed technical discussions with engineering teams.
- Demonstrated experience leading architecture governance and multidisciplinary delivery teams.
- Excellent communication and executive stakeholder management skills.

### Particularly Valuable Experience

- Hands-on experience with **VeriPark, VeriChannel and VeriLink**.
- Experience with **Central 1 Forge** and the Canadian credit union ecosystem.
- Experience migrating from Forge or another legacy digital banking platform to VeriPark.
- Experience with Backbase, ebankIT, Temenos, Intellect Design or other major digital banking platforms.
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform architecture.
- Relationships within the Canadian credit union, digital banking, or fintech ecosystem.
- Industry thought leadership, conference speaking, publishing, or participation in banking technology communities.

### What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you will have:

- Established yourself as a trusted architecture advisor to Aequilibrium's credit union clients.
- Successfully led architecture for one or more major digital banking transformations.
- Created reusable migration patterns and architecture assets that accelerate future implementations.
- Strengthened relationships with our digital banking technology partners.
- Helped Aequilibrium win additional digital banking transformation engagements.
- Mentored and elevated the architecture and engineering capabilities of the broader AEQ team.

### Compensation

This is a **contract role**, with a competitive rate of **CAD $80–$110/hour**, depending on experience, digital banking expertise, and demonstrated leadership capabilities.

For exceptional candidates with deep **VeriPark, Forge, and Canadian credit union experience**, compensation will reflect the strategic value and expertise they bring to Aequilibrium and our clients.

- Design, build, and optimize CRM architectures, workflows, automations, integrations, and connected data systems that support scalable revenue operations.  
- Develop enrichment, segmentation, routing, scoring, and lifecycle automation to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of revenue teams.  
- Monitor system health, troubleshoot technical issues, and continuously improve automation, data quality, governance, and platform performance.  
- Build reliable data flows and operational processes across multiple GTM platforms and ensure solutions are maintainable and scalable.  
- Collaborate with cross-functional specialists across paid media, content, delivery, and other functions to deliver cohesive technical solutions and strong partner outcomes.

- Advanced HubSpot experience and working knowledge of Clay are required.  
- Demonstrated experience designing and implementing scalable CRM architectures, workflows, and automation.  
- Experience building integrations, data flows, and operational processes across multiple go-to-market platforms.  
- Strong ability to translate business requirements, customer journeys, and strategic objectives into effective technical solutions.

- Strong systems thinking, with the ability to understand how data, processes, automation, and technology interact across the revenue lifecycle.  
- Ability to build reusable, maintainable solutions rather than relying on short-term fixes.

- Opportunity to grow within a rapidly expanding HubSpot-focused organization.  
- Collaborative environment focused on learning, innovation, ownership, and meaningful professional growth.
